key_insight: Composition-tuned site disorder in NiRuMnGa frustrates magnetic exchange, stabilizing a cluster-glass state instead of long-range magnetic order.
engineering_relevance: Tuning atomic disorder in quaternary Heusler alloys offers a route to engineer magnetic response, coercivity, and low-temperature functionality for spintronic and magnetic-device materials.
method: First-principles calculations to identify the energetically favorable crystal structure
Powder X-ray diffraction refinement using the calculated structure as the model
Magnetic characterization via dc, ac susceptibility, relaxation, memory, and heat-capacity measurements
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong ZFC-FC irreversibility near 48 K, unsaturated magnetization up to 7 T, slow spin dynamics, and no heat-capacity anomaly, collectively supporting cluster-glass behavior.
watch_item: The magnetic state is disorder-sensitive, so sample stoichiometry and site intermixing control will be critical for reproducibility and device integration.
paper_title: Role of composition-tuned disorder on magnetic exchange interactions in NiRuMnGa
